Israel killed 263 journalists over three years, Gaza media official says
articles.summary:
Israel killed 263 journalists over three years, Gaza media official says

The director of the Gaza Government Media Office said Israel has killed 263 journalists and media workers during its genocide. 

Ismail al-Thawabta told Anadolu Agency that 50 journalists had been detained in Israeli prisons, with 23 still in custody.

"Three journalists remain missing: Nidal Suheil al-Wahidi, Haitham Jamal Abdul Wahid and Ahmad Issam al-Agha," he added.

Thawabta said that Israeli attacks over the past three years have damaged or destroyed 16 satellite television offices, 11 radio institutions, 12 newspaper and magazine offices, 23 digital media organisations, 27 printing houses and five union and rights organisations involved in media work.

He estimated that the Gaza's media sector losses equaled to about $1 billion, including premises, equipment, broadcast vehicles and technical devices.

articles.title: Is Zionism Racism?
articles.summary:
Is Zionism Racism?

Britain's Green Party has declared Zionism a form of racism. The motion, passed at its Brighton conference by 1,022 votes to 813, makes the party officially anti-Zionist and backs a single democratic state in historic Palestine.
 
The reaction was fierce. Former leader Caroline Lucas spoke against it. Most Green MPs rejected it. Israel banned party leader Zack Polanski, though he did not vote. Much of the press called it “extremism”.
 
But what does Zionism actually mean? Does it mean different things to different people? And is branding Zionism "racism" a necessary premise to dismantle systems of oppression, or a missed opportunity?

Israeli anthropologist Jeff Halper, director of the Israeli Committee Against House Demolitions and co-founder of the One Democratic State Campaign, explains why he backs the motion’s substance, but thinks a diff headline could have achieved more.

Vance says Iran must cut nuclear enrichment capacity to reach deal with US
articles.summary:
Vance says Iran must cut nuclear enrichment capacity to reach deal with US

US Vice President JD Vance said that Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the war. 

"If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don't build highly enriched fuel. That's a very basic threshold issue," Vance said during an interview with Reuters.

"I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their enrichment capacity."

Vance also indicated that the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions. "We're not going to trade words for actions," he said.

articles.title: The agonising wait for Gaza’s missing
articles.summary:
The agonising wait for Gaza’s missing

Three years into Israel’s genocide in Gaza, Palestinian families are still searching for answers about thousands of relatives who vanished during the war.

Some disappeared during Israeli ground attacks on their neighbourhoods or displacement camps. Others went missing while searching for aid, checking on their homes or travelling near the so-called Yellow Line.

For their families, the absence of any definitive answer has left them suspended between hope and grief, unsure whether to keep waiting or begin mourning.

According to the Independent Commission for Human Rights, more than 11,000 people in Gaza remain unaccounted for, including those believed to be buried beneath the rubble and those suspected of enforced disappearance.

The Palestinian Centre for Missing and Forcibly Disappeared estimates that between 2,500 and 3,000 people are suspected of enforced disappearance, having gone missing or lost contact with their families since the start of the war and through the ceasefire announced on 9 October 2025.

Their fate remains unknown, with Israeli authorities still withholding the names of all those detained from the Strip and failing to identify approximately 620 bodies returned to Gaza.

Middle East Eye spoke to three families whose relatives disappeared during the war about their hopes, fears and the long wait for answers.

Read more: The agonising wait for Gaza’s missing

articles.summary: In 1975, the United Nations General Assembly adopted Resolution 3379 declaring Zionism “a form of racism and racial discrimination.” Sixteen years later, the resolution was revoked in the political context surrounding the Madrid Peace Conference. Western politics subsequently behaved as though the argument itself had been buried. It had not. History did not end in 1991, and neither did the political question the resolution raised. Today, that question has returned under circumstances far more devastating than those of 1975. Apartheid is no longer a term confined to Palestinian activists or to the margins of political debate. archive.security_status_en: The region faces elevated tensions following a thwarted hijacking attempt on a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv and mounting concerns over Iranian involvement. Meanwhile, Israeli security forces are reinforcing defenses in response to persistent threats from Gaza and potential escalation, while diplomatic engagements in Syria and Saudi Arabia signal ongoing regional realignments.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat detailnější vyšetřování incidentu s letem flydubai a pokračující politické manévrování v Izraeli před blížícími se volbami.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, more detailed investigations into the flydubai flight incident and continued political maneuvering in Israel ahead of upcoming elections are expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává vysoce napjatá v souvislosti s výročím událostí ze 7. října, přetrvávajícími neřešenými konflikty v Gaze a politickými třenicemi v Izraeli před blížícími se volbami. Diplomatická rétorika vůči Íránu navíc eskaluje kvůli jeho jadernému programu, což zvyšuje riziko širší eskalace.
archive.security_status_en: The regional security situation remains highly tense amid the anniversary of the October 7 events, ongoing unresolved conflicts in Gaza, and political friction in Israel ahead of upcoming elections. Additionally, diplomatic rhetoric regarding Iran's nuclear program is escalating, increasing the risk of broader confrontation.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zostřená bezpečnostní opatření v Izraeli a další diplomatické manévry ohledně íránského jaderného programu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heightened security measures in Israel and continued diplomatic maneuvering regarding Iran's nuclear program are expected.
